name: CA-20
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Vince Fong running with a large fundraising edge ($1.85M vs ~$17K)
Prediction markets price Fong at ~97% to win
No polling or expert ratings; fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: The district's R+16 lean, Fong's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing him near 97% all point to a safe Republican hold; the Democratic challenger has raised almost nothing.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Fong would be the only plausible signal of movement, but nothing currently suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Vince Fong, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to hold this Central Valley seat. The district leans Republican by sixteen points, and Fong enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised nearly $1.85 million while Democrat Sandra Van Scotter has raised about $17,000 and reports negative cash on hand. Prediction markets give Fong roughly a 97 percent chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. A Democratic upset would require a dramatic, unforeseen shift; the expected outcome is a comfortable Republican win on the order of seventeen points.
